Mostove Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mostove, Ukraine

Not demolished. This cemetery's oldest gravestone dates to 1831, with its older section presumably ruined during or after WWII; Mostove's Jews used the cemetery until at least 1992, and locals recall that 'respectful people,' including teachers and a school director, were buried there. The community existed by 1831 per cemetery dating; a synagogue operated from 1868, with population reaching 862 (54%) by 1897. 19th-and-early-20th-century Jews were mainly engaged in commerce - by 1914, the town's only pharmacy, two pharmacy-goods warehouses, and 15 market stalls were Jewish-owned. Population fell to 226 by 1939. Wehrmacht occupation from August 1941 established a ghetto; nearly 200 Jews were killed in January 1942, followed by a March 17, 1942 Aktion killing over 400 (including Bessarabian refugees), and roughly 900 more Mostove Jews and Transnistrian refugees executed during summer and autumn 1942. Cemetery dating confirms Jewish presence continued at least until 1992.
